Consensus by item, round and indicator

Source: R/consensus.R
delphi_consensus.Rd

Applies the interquartile-range (IQR) consensus criterion: an item reaches consensus when the IQR of the expert ratings is at most a given share of the rating scale, 20% by default (von der Gracht, 2012).

Usage

delphi_consensus(
  x,
  threshold = 0.2,
  relative_to = c("points", "range"),
  round = NULL,
  indicator = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  type = 7
)

Arguments

x

A delphi_data object.

threshold

Largest relative IQR that still counts as consensus, as a proportion between 0 and 1. Default 0.20.

relative_to

How the scale is measured: "points" (default) uses the number of scale points, max - min + 1; "range" uses max - min. See Details.

round, indicator, items

Optional subsets: round numbers, indicator labels and item names to keep. NULL keeps all.

type

Quantile algorithm passed to stats::quantile(); see delphi_describe().

Value

A data frame of class delphi_consensus with one row per indicator, round and item and columns indicator, round, item, n, median, q1, q3, iqr, iqr_rel, iqr_max (the largest IQR that counts as consensus on that scale) and consensus (TRUE, FALSE, or NA when there are no ratings). The rule is stored in the "rule" attribute.

Details

The relative IQR is \((Q_3 - Q_1) / w\), where \(w\) is the width of the scale. With the default relative_to = "points", the 20% threshold gives the cut-offs commonly reported in the literature reviewed by von der Gracht (2012): IQR \(\le 1\) on a five-point scale and IQR \(\le 2\) on a ten-point scale. With relative_to = "range" the cut-offs are slightly stricter (1.8 on a scale from 1 to 10); this choice is better suited to continuous scales, such as a scale from 0 to 100.

The rule should be fixed in the study protocol before data collection.

References

von der Gracht, H. A. (2012). Consensus measurement in Delphi studies: Review and implications for future quality assurance. Technological Forecasting and Social Change, 79(8), 1525-1536. doi:10.1016/j.techfore.2012.04.013

Examples

x <- delphi_data(delphi_example, expert_col = "expert",
                 round_col = "round", indicator_col = "indicator",
                 scale = list(impact = c(1, 10), plausibility = c(1, 100)))
cons <- delphi_consensus(x)
cons
#> Consensus rule: IQR <= 20% of the scale (number of points)
#> 
#>     indicator round item  n median    q1    q3   iqr iqr_rel iqr_max consensus

subset(cons, round == 2 & consensus)

# A stricter rule: IQR at most 10% of the scale
delphi_consensus(x, threshold = 0.10, round = 2)
